//: Config wrapper for the suspension bounce test: ride frequency and damping
//1: of each axle, the run docs/TODO.md 'Suspension spring/damper rate
//2: verification' asks for.  Needs a Chrono build:
//6: The car spawns 8 cm above its rest height on a flat rigid plane, wheels
//7: clear of the ground, and drops.  Nothing else happens: no key-on, no
//8: throttle, external_sim off, so the motion after touchdown is the free
//9: heave-and-pitch response of the two axles and nothing else.
//11: Two CSVs come out.  bounce_test_telemetry.csv (this file's telemetry
//12: block, 200 Hz) carries pos_z, the chassis reference height.  The
//13: scenario's scenario_bounce_test.csv carries pitch_deg every 5 ms.  Join
//14: them on time, then take the body height over each axle:
//16: z_front = pos_z + 1.346 * sin(pitch)    z_rear = pos_z - 1.166 * sin(pitch)
//18: 1.346 and -1.166 are the two 'Suspension Location' X values in
//20: rebound (about 0.5 s); from there each trace is a decaying oscillation
//21: about its rest height.  Ride frequency = 1 / mean period between
//22: successive upward crossings of the rest height; damping ratio from the
//23: log decrement of successive peaks, zeta = d / sqrt(4 pi^2 + d^2).
//25: What the suspension files predict, to compare against: rear 1.50 Hz at
//26: zeta 0.30 (EV1_RearFiveLink.json, the ev1 baseline's estimate); front
//27: about 1.8 Hz (EV1_FrontDoubleWishbone.json, unsourced rate on the sedan
//28: geometry).  Heave and pitch couple, so the two traces share some of
//29: each other's frequency; a clean reading needs both modes to settle,
//30: which is why the run is 6 s.
//32: Spawn height: at rest the spindles sit about one loaded tyre radius
//33: (0.275 m) above the plane and 0.29 m below the chassis reference, so
//34: the reference rests near z = 0.  Measure the rest height from the last
//35: second of the run rather than trusting that figure.
